newsitem.title: UK: UK's gas flexibility mechanism sells over weekend.
newsitem.headline: UK's gas flexibility mechanism sells over weekend.

text.p: The U.K.'s "flexibility mechanism" sold gas throughout the weekend, a spokeswoman for TransCo, the pipeline arm of British Gas Plc which operates the system told Reuters on Monday.
On Friday, there were 12 system sell bids accepted, totalling 104,262,385 kiloWatt (kw) hours (3.558 million therms), at an average price of 0.4027 pence per kw hour (around 11.80 pence a therm).

On Saturday, there were a further seven system sell bids accepted, totalling 60,644,546 kw hours (around 2.07 million therms) at an average price of 0.4178 pence per kw hour (around 12.245 pence a therm).

And on Sunday, nine system sell bids totalling 81,275,458 kw hours (around 2.773 million therms) were accepted. The average price fell to 0.388 pence per kw hour, or around 11.37 pence a therm -- considerably lower than recent prices for prompt gas on the spot market.
The flexibility mechanism has been in operation since the Network Code, the rulebook for users of TransCo's trunk gas pipeline system, came into effect in March.

Under the code, users are required to balance the volumes they put into the system against the volumes they take out on a daily basis. The flexibility mechanism allows them to do this electronically by leaving bids to buy or sell gas posted on a TransCo-operated computer link.
The spokeswoman said the fact three consecutive days of system sells were seen reflected mild weather, and consequent loss of demand, over the weekend.
